title: As a merchant, I can publish my product or service catalog into agent surfaces through a documented feed or import API so AI agents can discover what I sell
As an AI-native user, my agent can programmatically search products or services across merchants — keylessly or with self-service credentials, no private partnership required
As a developer, I can read machine-readable offer data — price, availability, variants, checkout links — for any listed product or service
As an AI-native user, my agent can discover payable services and APIs through a published directory or discovery index
As an AI-native user, my agent can create and update a cart or order draft through a documented protocol call
As an AI-native user, my agent can complete a purchase end-to-end — checkout session, delegated payment credential, confirmed order
As a developer, I can build against a versioned commerce protocol with a published schema and conformance or validation tooling
As a merchant, buyers can complete purchases of my products inside chat and assistant surfaces (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and peers)
As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number
As an AI-native user, I can provision a wallet my agent holds and spends from — funded and controlled by me, with balance visibility
As a developer, I can monetize an API or service with HTTP 402 machine payments that agents pay per call without a checkout UI
As a developer, I can settle agent-initiated payments in stablecoins over documented rails
As an AI-native user, sensitive agent spending requires my documented approval — a confirmation step, signed mandate, or per-purchase consent — before money moves
As a merchant, agents identify themselves verifiably — registered profiles, signatures, or trust tiers — so I can tell trusted agent traffic from anonymous bots
As an AI-native user, I can set per-agent spend caps and usage limits and revoke an agent's payment authority instantly
As a merchant, the fraud, liability, and chargeback rules for agent-initiated transactions are documented so I know who bears the risk
As a merchant, I have a documented self-serve path to start accepting agent traffic — enable a setting, sign an agreement, or publish an endpoint
As a merchant, orders are attributed to the originating agent and I can report on or filter transactions by agent
As a merchant, I can rate-limit, allow, or deny specific agents and agent platforms accessing my catalog and checkout
As a developer, my agent or backend can subscribe to order lifecycle events — created, updated, fulfilled, canceled — pushed programmatically
As an AI-native user, my agent can query the status and tracking of an order it placed, after the purchase
As a developer, refunds on agent-placed orders can be initiated and tracked programmatically
As a developer, disputes and chargebacks on agent transactions can be handled via API — evidence submission, status, outcomes
As a developer, the commerce protocol this product speaks is published as an open, versioned specification I can read and implement without signing anything
As a developer, at least two independent parties beyond the vendor implement the protocol or platform — it is an ecosystem, not a private integration
As a merchant, the fees for agent-originated transactions are published — I can price agentic channels without asking sales
As a merchant, agent-originated payments settle through documented payout and reporting flows, reconcilable like any other channel
